what: Favicon Generator makes the small icons that browsers show in tabs, bookmarks and on phone home screens. It creates a favicon.ico with three sizes inside, PNG versions, the Apple touch icon for iPhones and iPads, Android icons and the site.webmanifest file.

Start from your logo, from one to three letters on a coloured background, or from an emoji. Choose a square, rounded or round shape and the padding, and you see each size and a browser-tab preview straight away.
Download everything as a ZIP and copy the HTML code that tells browsers where to find the icons. All icons are made in your browser.
uses: Give a new site a proper icon instead of the blank default.
Make your tab and bookmark icon match your brand colours.
Get the 192 and 512 px icons and the manifest needed to install a web app on Android.
Use your initials or an emoji until a real logo is ready.
Rebuild all sizes from a larger logo so every icon is crisp.
Get the full set of files and HTML in seconds.
tutorial: Add your logo, letters or emoji
For Image, drop a square PNG, JPG or SVG. For Text, type 1 to 3 letters and pick a font and colour. For Emoji, type one or tap a popular one.
Pick "Shape" (square, rounded or circle), a "Background" colour or "See-through", and "Padding". For pictures, "Fit" shows the whole picture or fills the square.
Type the "Website name" and a "Theme colour". They go into site.webmanifest and the HTML.
The tab preview and the 16, 32, 48, 180 and 192 px previews update as you change things.
Unzip the files into the root folder of your website and paste the HTML from the box into the <head> of your pages.
features: ICO, PNG, Apple touch icon, Android icons and web manifest.
Three ways to start, with fonts and popular emoji.
Square, rounded or circle, with any background colour or see-through.
Icons are shrunk in steps for sharp 16 and 32 px results.
Copy the <link> and <meta> tags in one click.

example.title: Worked example: an icon from initials
example.text: Grace runs a bakery site called "Golden Toast". She has no logo yet, so she chooses Text, types GT, picks a rounded shape with a deep orange background and white letters. The 16 px preview is still readable. She types "Golden Toast" as the website name, presses "Download all (ZIP)", unzips the 9 files into her site's root folder and pastes the HTML into the head of her template. The next time she opens the site, the GT icon appears in the tab.

tips: Keep it simple: one bold letter or symbol is easier to recognise at 16 px than a detailed logo.
Use a background colour rather than see-through so the icon shows clearly on both light and dark browser tabs.
Browsers cache favicons for a long time. Open the icon file directly or use a private window to see the new one.
Add a little padding for round shapes so letters do not touch the edge.
problems: My new favicon does not show
Browsers keep old icons for a while. Check the files are in the root folder, then reload with Ctrl+F5 or open a private window.
Use a bigger source picture, at least 512 × 512 px, or an SVG.
The emoji looks different on another device
Emoji are drawn by each device's own emoji font. The icon files keep the look from the device you made them on.
Choose "Show the whole picture" in "Fit" and add some padding.
